content:
President Donald Trump praised Chinese leader Xi Jinping at length on Thursday for greeting him at the airport upon his arrival for a summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin — and critics say he’s being made the fool.

Trump — when asked by Fox News’ Jacqui Heinrich what headline he wants to come out of the trilateral meeting — said he’s already got a headline in the form of his “great” relationship with China as seen in Beijing’s grand state welcome for him.

“You saw the seating [at the banquet] last night, you saw the greeting yesterday, which in the history of China has never happened, no president has ever — and this is a highly respected, this is a great president, one of the great presidents of China,” he said of Xi personally receiving him at the airport, a notably rare move.

He went on to remark on more of the welcome that featured groups of young people on the tarmac dressed in bright colors holding flowers along with both the U.S. and Chinese flags.

“The fanfare, the beauty, the pageantry, the thousands of people, the young children, the soldiers, the whole thing. It was a great respect and I appreciate that,” he said.

“That’s a big win for us. That’s a big win for China, too. We get along.”

Xi — in what was reportedly the first such instance by China’s leader in decades— greeted a foreign leader upon their arrival to the country on Wednesday when he welcomed Trump on the tarmac, shaking hands with him and briefly hugging him while standing on a red carpet. (Xi didn’t greet Trump in such a way upon his visit to China in May, nor did he personally welcome Putin on Wednesday.)

It marked Xi’s way of reciprocating Trump welcoming him upon his arrival to America back in September, itself an unusual move for a U.S. president.

Critics on social media ripped Trump over his notion of a “big win” including Fox News’ liberal host Jessica Tarlov, who wrote on X, “We made a man who is so easily manipulated our president TWICE!”

Filmmaker Morgan J. Freeman also dismissed the president’s suggestion, noting that Xi said he was “simply returning the courtesy” Trump extended him in September.

“That’s called diplomatic protocol, Donald. Not a trade deal. Not lower prices. Not a victory for American families,” he wrote. “A red carpet isn’t a foreign policy achievement.”

And another user put it this way, morphing the president’s quote to read, “‘I love being played like a fiddle and being too stupid to know the difference.’”
